hook_text: Every cyclist in this race is wearing two helmets. You can only see one of them.
clip_script: Race morning in Cape Town. Thousands of riders clip on their helmets. But under every helmet is another one: the skull, a hard case around the soft brain. Down the back, the backbone wraps the spinal cord in a tunnel of bone. Around the chest, twelve pairs of ribs guard the heart and lungs. And the leg bones? The strongest in the body, pushing those pedals. Your skeleton holds you up, keeps you safe and helps you move.
visual_style: Whiteboard cyclist turning into an outline skeleton, with skull, backbone and ribs glowing as they are named.
mood: Energetic, like the start of a race.
pacing: Three protection stops from head to chest, then a fast finish with the legs pedalling.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and gently feel your ribs and backbone.
